JUDGMENT
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road accident on 17.12.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 17.12.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., the petitioner was finishing SCCH-24 her work and went to deposit her collection amount Depot department, at that time while entering the office very carefully, casually observing traffic rules, at that time rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HL9477 came with rash and negligent manner, which endangours to human life and dashed against her, due to impact she fell down and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.

Immediately she was shifted to Vijayashree Hospital, Jigani,
Bangalore wherein admitted as an inpatient and discharged with an advise.
So far she has spent a sum of Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses, conveyances, food and nourishment charges other incidental charges.
3. It is further submitted that prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, was working as conductor in BMTC and getting a salary of Rs.30,539/ per month.
After the accident she was unable to work as early, she was lost her income, and suffering lot mentally, physically and financially.
The Jigani Police have registered a case against SCCH-24 the rider of motorcycle bearing reg.No.KA51HL9477 in crime No.209/2020 u/Sec.279, 337 of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the owner and the 2 nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents have appeared through their respective counsel and filed separate written statements.

5. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement denied the averments made in para No.1 to 22 of the claim petition as false and submitted that the petitioner is trying to make wrongful gain by filing this claim petition on the wrong parties.

Further submitted that she is the owner of the vehicle bearing No.KA51HL9477 and the same is insured with the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company and the rider of the alleged vehicle was having an effective driving license at the time of accident,
hence she is not SCCH-24 liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against her.

Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
2 6.

The Respondent No.2 in the written statement have denied the averments made in column no.1 to 4, 8 to 14 and 22 as false, admitted the issuance of policy but subject to its terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Section 134(c) of M.V. Act and the alleged accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the petitioner as she was crossing the road, unmindful of the traffic, that too at a place not earmarked for pedestrian crossing.

Further submitted that the petitioner being an employee of BMTC is entitled for ESI medical facility and the entire medical expenses would have been reimbursed under the said scheme by the Government.
The petitioner has availed paid leave and has not suffered any loss of earnings.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
SCCH-24 7.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed :
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that, she met with a Road Traffic accident on 17.12.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., infront of Jigani BMTC Depot, on Jigani OTS circle Jigani APC circle, Jigani Town and Hobali, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District and sustained grievous injuries due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA 51HL9477?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?
8. The Petitioner in order to prove her case, she has examined herself as PW.1 and marked 13 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.13.
Dr.Chidanand K.J.C got examined as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Exs.P14 and P15.
On the other side the Respondents did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.
SCCH-24 9.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for both the parties.

10. On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on records this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 11. Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HL9477 has examined herself as PW.1 and produced documents as per Exs.P.1 to P6 and P8.

She has specifically stated in her evidence that, on 17.12.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., she was finishing her work and went to deposit her collection SCCH-24 amount Depot department, at that time while entering the office very carefully, casually observing traffic rules, at that time rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
3 51HL9477 came with rash and negligent manner, which endangers to human life and dashed against her and caused accident, due to impact she fell down and sustained multiple injuries all over the body.
On the other side, the Respondents have contended that the alleged accident was taken place only due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.
But to prove their defence the Respondents have not lead any independent evidence but relied on the admission of the PW.1 and the police documents.
In the cross examination of the PW.1 it is elicited that there was no any pedestrian crossing or any provision made for pedestrians where she was crossing the road.
12. The PW.1 clearly admitted that she was crossing the road where it was not earmarked for pedestrian crossing.

Further, apart from oral evidence the petitioners SCCH-24 have produced the Ex.P.1 is the FIR in Cr.No.209/2020 of Jigani Police Station which registered after receipt of first information, the Ex.P.2 complaint, Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar drawn in the said case, Ex.P.4 is the MVA report, Ex.P.5 is the police intimation, Ex.P.6 is the statement of the witnesses in Cr.N.209/2020 of Jigani Police station and Ex.P8 is the true copy of chargesheet filed by the Petitioner
clearly discloses that it filed against the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA51 HL9477 as he caused accident in which the petitioner sustained injuries.

Therefore, on appreciating the said documents which are public documents having presumptive value under law and on appreciating the evidence of PW.1 this Tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner was also contributed to the alleged accident which can be assessed at 25%.
The wound certificate produced by the Petitioner as per Ex.P.7 clearly discloses that due to the accident the Petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Under these circumstances, as SCCH-24 per the discussion made above this Tribunal is of the opinion that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA51HL9477 alongwith contributory negligence of the petitioner and same has resulted in grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held partly in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:

The Petitioner has further averred that on account of the accidental injuries now she cannot discharge her duty effectively, happiness earning capacity and not able to do work as earlier as the injuries are caused permanent disability and hence she is unable to do her earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries she is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, she has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.7.

As per Ex.P.7, the Petitioner has sustained right leg SCCH-24 both bones fracture, mild head injury with CLW, left leg lower third degloving injury and left inferior pubic rami fracture, the doctor opined that the injuries are grievous in nature.

The Ex.P.9/Discharge summary issued by Vijayashree Hospital, it shows that the petitioner has admitted as an inpatient from 17.12.2020 to 22.12.2020 and underwent CRIF with IL IM nailing under SA on 18.12.2020 and also examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C as PW.2.

This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle along with the contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.

Disability:
Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
4 14.

In the chiefexamination, PW.2 has deposed that a patient by name Madhura H.J. aged about 43 years came to our hospital on 29.07.2022 with alleged history of RTA SCCH-24 and did sustain right leg both bone fracture, mild head injury, left leg lower third degloving injury with CLW and left inferior pubic rami fracture and underwent surgery in form of CRIF with IMIL nailing in Vajayshree Hospital,
Bangalore and other injuries are treated conservatively.

He has further deposed that on 29.07.2022 patient came for disability assessment and it is noted healed surgical scar mark over right knee, mild swelling of left and right leg, ankle, altered pigmentation over the surgical scar mark, thickening of bone right leg felt, range of movements of right knee and ankle, restricted, daily activities cross leg sitting,
squatting for using Indian toilets were found to be difficulty and xray right leg show fracture united with implant in situ and left hip shows fracture pubic rami mal united and the petitioner has got permanent physical disability for right lower limb is 44% and to the whole body is 15%.
Further PW.2 deposed that, patient will have difficulties in daily routine activities too and requires one SCCH-24 more surgery for implant removal at approximate cost of Rs.20,000/.

In the crossexamination of PW.2 it is brought out that, fractures are united, the implants needs to be removed from the fracture site of operated one fracture and other two fractures were treated conservatively and except removal of implant he has not advised any further treatment.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment that she has undergone and her age, the functional disability of the petitioner is considered at 10% to the whole body.
As per the evidence of PW.1 she continued in the same service and getting salary and hence it is clear that there is no functional disability to the petitioner.

Monthly income:
15.
The petitioner has stated in his evidence that, she was working as a conductor in BMTC and getting salary of Rs.30,539/ per month.
In this regard she has produced salary slips for the month of July and August 2021 with SCCH-24 endorsement at Ex.P11 but has not examined her employer.
In the cross examination of PW.1 she admitted that she has continued her services.
Though the petitioner states that she was on leave and suffered loss of pay but has not lead any specific evidence in this regard.

Therefore, from this evidence it is clear that there is no loss of income to the petitioner and also not suffered any financial loss during the laidup period due to disability and it is also clear that the petitioner not suffers any functional disability.
Under these circumstances the question of calculating the loss of future income due to disability does not arise.

As such, Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation:
i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:

After the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Vijayashree Hospitals,
Anekal Tq, wherein admitted as an inpatient on 17.12.2020 to 22.12.2020 for 6 days as per Ex.P.9.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and SCCH-24 duration of treatment she has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.80,000/ under this head.

Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
5 ii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:

The petitioner claimed that she incurred Rs.3,00,000/ towards medical expenses and produced prescriptions and 22 medical bills for Rs.1,67,968/, 34 Medical bills amounting to Rs.1,70,139/ and 8 prescriptions at Exs.P10, P12 and P13.

In the cross examination of PW.1 though she has denied that she got ESI benefit and stated that the medical advances mentioned in the Ex.P.11/salary slips are the advances and has to be repaid each month.
On perusal of the endorsement dated 31.07.2021 issued by Chief Labor and Welfare Officer it shows that they have paid medical expenses and also the salary for the leave period.

The said endorsement further shows that a direction is issued to the petitioner to get reimbursement of said medical expenses SCCH-24 and salary in the claim and to remit it to their Corporation but in order to support the said document the petitioner has not chosen to examine her employer or the issuer of said endorsement.

From the endorsement itself it is clear that the Corporation has paid the medical expenses to the petitioner and hence in absence of any specific evidence that she is not entitled to get medical expenses by her Corporation and if any such medical expenses is borne then it needs to be claimed and repaid to the Corporation, the said endorsement cannot be appreciated in favour of the petitioner.
Further, on perusal of the medical bills they do not bear the signature of the issuer but only seal is put in some of the medical bills.

When the aforesaid endorsement clearly states that the Corporation has paid the medical expenses to the petitioner then how the petitioner has produced the medical bills before this Tribunal is not explained and from this it is clear that this medical bills are not the original but are the second set.
Therefore, the SCCH-24 petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
iii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:

As mentioned above she has sustained right leg both bones fracture, mild head injury with CLW, left leg lower third degloving injury and left inferior pubic rami fracture, which are grievous in nature.
The petitioner was admitted to Vijayashree Hospital, as an inpatient from 17.12.2020 to 22.12.2020, took treatment for 6 days and took follow up treatment.

The petitioner has not produced any documents to support her claim that she took leave and was not paid with the salary or she suffered loss of EL and hence the claim of the petitioner that she did not get salary for the leave period is not acceptable as the endorsement issued by their Corporation itself clearly shows that the petitioner was paid with the salary for the leave period.

In absence of specific evidence of employer of the petitioner about the SCCH-24 leave taken by her and nonpayment of salary the claim of the petitioner cannot be acceptable that she sustained loss of leave.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:

In the crossexamination the PW.1 clearly stated that she continued as Conductor in the Corporation and getting salary and hence it is clear that there is no any functional disability to the petitioner and there is also no loss of income to her.
Therefore, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation under this head.
v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 41 years at the time of accident.
She has sustained right leg both bones fracture, mild head injury with CLW, left leg lower third degloving injury and left inferior pubic rami fracture, which is SCCH-24 grievous in nature.

As per the evidence of PW.2 and consideration of this Tribunal, she is suffering from 10%
permanent physical disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Because of this she will have to loose many amenities and comforts.

Therefore, considering the age Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
6 and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded under this head.
vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT CHARGES:

After the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to the Vijayashree Hospital, Anekal Tq,
wherein she took treatment as an inpatient for 6 days.
During this period she must have spent considerable amount on her conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc,. and no contrary evidence is lead.
Therefore, considering the same the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
SCCH-24 vii)
FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.2, the Petitioner is advised to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants at approximate cost of Rs.20,000/.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.2.

Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and cross examination of PW.2,
it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
Therefore the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.

16. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.80,000/
2.

Medical expenses ---- 3. Loss of income during laid up period  4. Loss of future income  5. Loss of future amenities and happiness Rs.50,000/
6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.20,000/ nourishment charges 7.
Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/ TOTAL Rs.1,60,000/ SCCH-24

The total compensation comes to Rs.1,60,000/ and if the 25% negligence is deducted then the remaining compensation comes to Rs.1,20,000/ (Rs.1,60,000/  Rs.40,000/
).

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,20,000/
alongwith interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

LIABILITY:
Smt.Madhura H.J vs Varalakshmamma on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55956514/
7 17.
The Respondent No.2 has not proved its other defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are being the owner and the Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.2 - insurer has got primary liability to compensate the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.50,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,20,000/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
SCCH-24
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The petition is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,20,000/ (Rupees One Lakh Twenty Thousand only) from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents 1 SCCH-24 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this Judgment.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire compensation shall be released in favour of the Petitioner on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per Rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.

Draw decree accordingly.
